evidence: src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts open(): `throw new FleetError(`${plate} already has an open work order`, 409)` gives the domain error HTTP 409 Conflict, a status code the delivery layer should choose
src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts vehicle(): `throw new FleetError(`Unknown vehicle ${plate}`, 404)` gives the domain error HTTP 404 Not Found
src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts order(): `throw new FleetError(`Unknown work order ${id}`, 404)` gives the domain error HTTP 404 Not Found
The constructor injects VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable from the persistence layer, which business may depend on, so this wiring is allowed
parsedVerdict.reasoning: MaintenanceService is in the business layer, which is a domain layer. Its persistence calls go through VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable, which come from the persistence layer it is allowed to depend on, and they are passed in through the constructor. So they are allowed dependency wiring, not misplaced I/O. It has no framework decorators, base classes or ORM types. The orchestration and domain rules (one open order per vehicle, taking a vehicle out of service and returning it, overrun) suit the domain. However, the service throws FleetError carrying HTTP status codes: 409 (Conflict) for a duplicate open order and 404 (Not Found) for an unknown vehicle or work order. Choosing an HTTP response status is the job of the delivery layer (WorkshopController), so the domain service is doing presentation work. Confidence is moderate because FleetError is the project's own business-layer type and the codes are plain number literals rather than imports from a web package.

violations.message: The domain service throws FleetError with HTTP status codes (409 in open(), 404 in vehicle() and order()). Mapping errors to HTTP status codes belongs to the presentation layer (WorkshopController), not the business/domain layer.
